entry_conditions: The peg remains in the box or is already securely moving with closed fingers. Use for an early or late incoming switch when two causal frames expose the actual TCP, joints, fingers, lid, and peg state and only modest local correction is needed.
exit_conditions: A sequence of local lift targets has put the observed, co-moving peg above the wall; initial transport or turn may already be underway within the outgoing overlap.
overlap_role: All 210 incoming overlap actions [740,950) and 150 outgoing overlap actions [1120,1270) per trajectory are action-supervised. TCP-relative targets can continue shared behavior from the measured hand pose rather than an assumed boundary pose.
successor_readiness: Switch to reorient_and_stage_peg when closed fingers and approximately stable peg/TCP relative pose persist while the peg moves above the box wall. The full outgoing lift overlap provides shared labels.
failure_signatures: Local targets oscillate or accumulate drift; peg-relative alignment fails to improve; fingers close while offset; peg does not rise with TCP; a large peg displacement demands increments outside support; or IK repeatedly fails or reaches joint limits.
continuation_guidance: Use this local-state specialist for modest incoming hand-pose mismatch and replan every eight actions. Prefer retrieve_peg_from_box__h01 for clear peg displacement and retrieve_peg_from_box__h03 for early lid-versus-peg phase ambiguity. Do not infer contact from closure alone.
limitations: This is learned local behavior, not a certified controller or recovery policy. Repeated chunks can accumulate translation/orientation error. There is no contact truth and no failed-pickup supervision.
